narrative.overview:
A browser development studio presented as a working canvas. Pale mineral mint space, deep forest ink and emerald actions let code and its visible result lead. The page is the proof: a real editor frame, a real command palette, a real file tree, a real live preview — each one composed in CSS rather than photographed.

The system is quiet by construction. Surfaces are separated by hairline rules and tonal fields, not by heavy cards. Reading rows stay open and ruled; filled rounded surfaces are reserved for things that behave like objects. One emerald accent carries every action, every selected state and every active rule, and it appears on less than a tenth of any screen.

Self-hosted Manrope keeps the voice modern and professional; a system monospace marks code, paths and measurements. Rounded controls are softly squared rather than pill-shaped, so the studio chrome reads as tooling and not as a consumer app.
keyCharacteristics: One mineral mint and emerald palette across every surface
Hairline rules and open rows instead of nested card stacks
A single drawn icon system: 24×24 grid, 1.75px stroke
Accessible tab semantics and keyboard selection in the studio

rules.name: The Shared Palette Rule
rules.body: Every adapted library component consumes the marketing semantic tokens. A second palette never enters the site, and no component carries its own accent color.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Emerald is the only chroma. It marks actions, selection and active state, and nothing else. Its rarity is the point.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: Structure is expressed with 1px rules and tonal fields. A shadow alone never carries a layout decision.

rules.name: The Tracking Floor Rule
rules.body: Headings never track below -0.035em. Body copy and labels track at zero.

rules.name: The One Measure Rule
rules.body: Prose never exceeds 72 characters. A measure that gets wider is a measure that stops being read.

rules.name: The Ambient Rule
rules.body: Every shadow carries an offset and a soft blur. A zero-offset halo is decoration, not depth.

rules.name: The Restrained Shadow Rule
rules.body: At most one stage-level shadow is visible in a viewport. Shadows never stack.

rules.name: The One Radius Language Rule
rules.body: Every radius comes from the documented scale. A new corner value is a design-system decision, not a local choice.

dos: Do use the shared semantic tokens in every Astro page, React island and adapted library component.
Do draw icons from the shared registry so stroke weight never drifts.
Do keep white foregrounds on filled emerald calls to action, including links inside reading sections.
Do place titles before taxonomy metadata, and let a heading carry its own weight without a label above it.
Do preserve visible keyboard focus, real tab semantics and reduced-motion behavior.
Do preserve all nine languages, every article and every route when extending the system.
donts: Don't reintroduce kickers, eyebrows or other labels above a heading.
Don't introduce a second accent, a second icon weight or a per-library palette.
Don't use emoji, Unicode glyphs or a second icon family as decoration.
Don't present illustrative code, the terminal study or the IDE frame as a live session.
Don't stack filled rounded surfaces inside each other; use rules for reading content.
Don't infer a visual identity for the separate application from this marketing system.
